plain_language: Anthropic opened Milan and Seoul offices; its AI surfaced 10,000 flaws. SpaceX filing and Musk diverge by $37B on the Anthropic compute deal. Figure now builds one humanoid per hour as June fills up.
findings:
Saturday's evidence cycle resolves into four tightly stacked threads, three of which validate yesterday's fresh predictions inside their first post-trigger trading day, two of which land structurally distinct dormant longshots back on the active board, and one of which carries forward the Bay Area June calendar at higher resolution than any prior cycle this week. The Anthropic geographic-footprint plus Project Glasswing first-update bundle is the structural anchor of the cycle. Inside 48 hours either side of Thursday's Series H close, Anthropic appointed KiYoung Choi (formerly Country Manager of Snowflake Korea) as Representative Director of Korea on Tuesday May 26 and opened a Milan office on Wednesday May 27 — its sixth European footprint after London, Dublin, Paris, Zurich, and Munich — under GDPR-compliant data residency, with senior leadership traveling to Seoul in coming weeks to formally open that office. The Project Glasswing first-update that flowed through trade press the same week credited Claude Mythos Preview with 10,000-plus high- or critical-severity findings across roughly 50 partners (Mozilla closed 271 Firefox vulnerabilities at ten times its prior rate, Cloudflare surfaced 2,000 bugs of which 400 were rated high or critical), 530 disclosures to maintainers, and 75 patches completed, plus a wolfSSL CVE-2026-5194 certificate-forgery flaw at CVSS 9.1 sitting on a TLS library embedded across roughly five billion IoT, automotive, and industrial-control devices. The geographic-footprint depth across Europe and Korea is exactly the international-operations posture the Anthropic confidential S-1 prediction (May 29) names as the structural force the prospectus risk-factor section needs to disclose against EU AI Act, GDPR, and Korean PIPC compliance perimeters, and the Glasswing quantitative disclosure (10k findings, 530 maintainer disclosures, 75 patches, five-billion-device blast radius on one CVE) hardens the frontier-lab governance frameworks convergence prediction (May 29) as a second Tier-1 lab numeric posture printing inside 48 hours of OpenAI's Friday Frontier Governance Framework.

The SpaceX S-1 versus Musk $37.5 billion Memphis Colossus disclosure-gap thread crystallizes the IPO-prospectus disclosure axis with structurally distinct read-through against three separate predictions. The SpaceX May 20 S-1 describes Anthropic as agreeing to pay a $1.25 billion monthly fee through May 2029 — implying a roughly $45 billion three-year commitment — while Musk said on X the arrangement is a 180-day lease with 90-day mutual cancellation putting maximum obligation at roughly $7.5 billion, and adding that SpaceX may reclaim capacity for xAI if compute gets super tight. The underlying asset is Memphis Colossus 1 with more than 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs across 300-plus megawatts originally built to train Grok, and SpaceX confirmed the SPCX ticker on Nasdaq with the institutional roadshow opening Monday June 8 at a $1.75 trillion-to-$2 trillion target range and roughly $75 billion raise, pricing scheduled June 11 and first trade June 12. The collision previews the multi-year-AI-compute-prebuy footnote structure every accelerator-pure-play S-1 will draft into across June and July — directly relevant to the Anthropic S-1 counterparty-symmetry language, to the Tenstorrent S-1 customer-disclosure section (May 24), and to the SEC 8-K cyber materiality concept-release window the agentic-AI dev-tool prediction (May 26) names. The dormant hyperscaler-AI-lab capital coupling thesis (April 26) revives at coherence 4 with the structural read that Anthropic's compute substrate now spans hyperscaler runtimes plus a non-hyperscaler SpaceX-controlled GPU cluster with explicit reclaim rights — a fourth coupling form strictly broader than the original Google-Amazon-Microsoft hyperscaler-cohort fact pattern this dormant longshot anticipated.

The Figure AI BotQ disclosure delivers the cleanest dormant-revival pair of the cycle and the day's highest-coherence support for two parallel physical-AI longshots. Figure AI on Wednesday May 27 disclosed that its BotQ manufacturing facility scaled Figure 03 production from one robot per day to one robot per hour over the prior 120 days — a 24-times throughput improvement — pushing total shipments past 350 units across more than 10 product variants, with 55 robots planned for the week and over 9,000 actuators produced, leaning on 150-plus workstations distributed across dedicated assembly lines plus custom manufacturing software plus tightened supplier quality controls that pushed first-pass yields above 80 percent. The Physical AI 8-hour production runs becoming enterprise RFP cuts thesis (April 24) revives at coherence 4 with a Figure-anchored second OEM-cohort throughput-and-yield data point sitting alongside Apptronik's Apollo Generation 2 ten-unit Mercedes-Benz Tuscaloosa cohort clearing 120-hour zero-MTBF preflight earlier in the week, and the Physical AI league tables ranking top-five OEM-adopted humanoids thesis (April 25) revives at coherence 4 with three named pure-play humanoid OEM-adoption counts (Figure 03 with 350+ shipments at 80% first-pass yield, Apptronik Apollo Gen 2 with its 10-unit Tuscaloosa preflight, Tesla Optimus Gen 3 with its summer-2026 Fremont production-start target) now printing publishable comparable metrics inside a single 14-day window. The procurement-RFP-cut consequence and the league-table consequence both depend on at least three named comps with publishable yield and throughput metrics — the Saturday Figure print pulls the third anchor count into the same publishable-metrics regime as Apptronik and Optimus rather than the still-pre-revenue cohort.

The Bay Area June-July calendar carries forward at higher resolution than any prior compose-summary cycle this week, with the May-31/June-6 registration-deadline hinge brackets pulling the OECD GENAI plenary June 2-6 closing-session window into the same regulator-facing attention surface. Snowflake Summit 26 opens Monday June 1-4 at Moscone with the 5:00 PM PT keynote pairing Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy with Anthropic President Daniela Amodei before 20,000-plus attendees, Microsoft Build 2026 follows Tuesday-Wednesday June 2-3 at Fort Mason San Francisco with the Windows Agent Framework slated for open-source MIT-licensed release on day one alongside Copilot Agent Mode and a Windows Agent Store marketplace, WWDC26 keynotes Monday June 8, Databricks Data + AI Summit runs Moscone June 15-18 with 800-plus sessions and named Microsoft, OpenAI, NVIDIA, Anthropic, and LangChain speakers, and AI Engineer World's Fair caps the wave Moscone West June 29-July 2 with 250-plus speakers across 20-plus tracks including Agentic Commerce, Inference, Security, Generative Media, and Harness Engineering. The Microsoft Build MIT-licensed Windows Agent Framework opening-day release is exactly the first-party orchestrator landing inside the five-week venue cohort that the open-source orchestrator 1k-parallel-subagent prediction (May 29) names as the surface where bounded-parallel primitive announcements are most likely to print between now and Q4 — the open-source side now has a Microsoft-shipped reference framework with a marketplace surface to bind against, in addition to the Anthropic Dynamic Workflows ceiling reference. Three dormant longshots reviving on a single Saturday (Physical AI 8-hour runs, Physical AI league tables, hyperscaler-AI-lab capital coupling) is unusual signal density — the Memphis Colossus disclosure-gap thread plus the Figure BotQ throughput print plus the Bay Area June calendar pulls a Saturday-news-thin day into a structurally dense cross-stream cycle anchored on physical-AI cohort revivals and the hyperscaler-coupling axis broadening.
